Associate Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg walks on stage to receive an honorary degree at the University at Buffalo on Monday, Aug. 26, 2019. (Mark Mulville/Buffalo News)

By Sandra Tan

Published Mon, Aug 26, 2019|Updated Mon, Aug 26, 2019

U.S. Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg received a standing ovation this morning when she stepped on stage at the University at Buffalo to receive an honorary degree.

Her appearance at the Center for the Arts on the North Campus in Amherst was the beginning of a day of events for Ginsburg, who recently underwent treatment for a malignant tumor discovered on her pancreas.

She was scheduled to answer questions from students before meeting with members of the UB Law School this afternoon. Her day also includes a speech at Kleinhans Music Hall later today.

"It's an immense honor to host Justice Ginsburg at the University at Buffalo," UB President Satish Tripathi said Monday. "During her trailblazing career, she has had, and continues to have, a transformative impact on society."

Ginsburg, an associate justice on the court since 1993, was invited to Buffalo last year by local attorney Wayne D. Wisbaum, a friend from their college days at Cornell University. Wisbaum died in December and her visit is dedicated to his memory.

"This visit is both a joy and a sorrow for me," Ginsburg said of Wisbaum in her first remarks to the crowd.

Aviva Abramovsky, the dean of UB's Law School, interviewed Ginsburg on stage, asking her why she decided to become an attorney and what women inspired her (Amelia Earhart and Nancy Drew).

Long before she was even scheduled to take the stage, seats in the Center for the Arts were filling up.

"We're very excited, especially since today is Women's Equality Day," said third year law student Meghan Carrig.

The UB event was open only to faculty, students and staff. Tickets to the sold out event went fast.

"I was on a wait list," said Debbie Lowe, who works in the UB School of Management. "I was able to get one ticket."

"She's a very famous figure," Lowe added. "I love what she stands for. I hope she'll be here for another 25 years."

Ginsburg, a Brooklyn native, studied law at Harvard and Columbia universities, graduating first in her class in 1959, but no New York City law firms would offer a job to a woman. During the 1970s, she argued a number of women’s rights cases at the Supreme Court.

Recently, Ginsburg's profile has risen through the movie "On the Basis of Sex," the documentary "RBG" and "Saturday Night Live" parodies.

"To see her speak is the opportunity of a lifetime," said Eileen Marutiak Yildirim, an alumna and member of the Alumni Association's board of directors.

"I'm excited just to be in the same room as her," said third year law student Erica Chiodo.

It was announced on Friday that Ginsburg underwent treatment this summer for a malignant tumor discovered on her pancreas.

"I did not withdraw (from the Buffalo visit) when my own health issues presented problems," she said Monday at UB.
